isogenic_exception.statement: ADR 0066 Isogenic exception: the six in-vitro hiPSC-CM models carry a patient genotype with an isogenic control and are kept as their own evidence type inside this category even though a human CM-pseudobulk cohort (Reichart-CM) exists for the same category: a mixed-etiology clinical cohort and a single-genotype isogenic model answer different questions, and collapsing them loses the causal signature. The category therefore has one tier-1 human CM-pseudobulk pair (Reichart genotype-positive DCM + ARVC) and six tier-2 isogenic bulk datasets; `tier` records the winning tier and each dataset record carries its own `evidence_type` and `tier`.

rejected.reason: eligible isogenic HCM MYBPC3 deposit, but its control sets are batch confounded and the six isogenic models already cover MYBPC3 HCM
eligible isogenic bulk models, but the declared roster fixes the six isogenic accessions; admitting more would exceed the survey fetch list
ARVC DSP models: GSE289628 is confounded by AAV6-vs-siRNA vehicle and GSE248187 deposits a DEG table only, so no counts could be re-fit
ADR 0066 does not use the NCCM donor; it is excluded from the tracked export and appears in no dataset of this category

tiering.rule: the tier-stop criterion is the disease DEG union resolved to the frozen 18,164-gene axis (axis-resolved, not genome-wide): a source DEG off the axis cannot enter DEG2000 or any axis built from it, so it does not count toward the 2,000-gene stop test. Sources are collected in ascending tier order; a tier with no declared source is absent from the ladder (AF declares tier 1 and tier 3, no tier 2), and a category whose evidence begins at tier 2 (the cardiotox classes) enters there. The cumulative axis-resolved union is measured after each tier and collection stops at the first tier whose union reaches the limit; a declared source in a deeper tier after a completed tier that already reached the limit is refused rather than admitted. Only declared sources are collected, so a tier between two entered tiers is never back-filled.
